answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed if peers prove fraud, so spawning thousands of fake identities costs real capital instead of free keystrokes. Like a vine that only thrives where it has genuinely put down roots, an agent's reputation should grow only through a verifiable history of completed work, not self-declared claims. New identities start in a dune of low trust and must earn their way toward the oasis of high-value contracts through sustained, attested performance.
